abstract: The Flow Matching objective supervises the velocity field at intermediate states, whereas waveform metrics are evaluated after decoding and may be non-differentiable. To align Flow Matching models with waveform-level and perceptual quality objectives during post-training, FlowGRPO optimizes their trajectories using endpoint rewards. In this work, we focus on music separation and use multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform (MRSTFT), scale-invariant signal-to-distortion ratio (SI-SDR), and Virtual Speech Quality Objective Listener (ViSQOL) as reward components. Before policy optimization, we analyze the relationship between data quality factors and the within-group gap between the maximum and mean rollout rewards for each component. This analysis motivates a revised ViSQOL reward that matches channel-wise root-mean-square (RMS) levels and evaluates the interval from the first to the last active frame, retaining inactive frames within that interval. We also apply a sample-quality filter based on predefined waveform checks. Together, the revised reward and quality filter enable FlowGRPO to improve the pretrained vocal separator in both separation performance and perceptual quality.

oneSentenceThesis: 该文研究潜空间流匹配人声分离在波形指标不可微时的后训练对齐，用组内最优与均值差距分析指导 ViSQOL 改写与样本过滤，使 FlowGRPO 在原评价指标上提升分离与感知质量，但结论只在内部 50 秒测试与固定阈值下成立且 MRSTFT 单奖励仍保留最低谱损失。
